title: Overnight backup job failed
symptom: The nightly backup job has failed three nights in a row
user_description: The backup alerts have been red since Monday. I haven't had time to look. Can you take it?

options.text: Ignore it for now because older backups still exist
options.why: Every failed night is data that cannot be recovered if something goes wrong today.

options.text: Delete old backups to make room, without checking
options.why: Old backups may be needed for retention rules, and the failure may not even be about space.

options.text: Read the job log to find the error, fix the cause (for example a full destination or expired credentials), run the job manually, confirm it completes, then test restoring a file
options.why: The log tells you why it failed. A backup is only proven good when a restore works.

options.text: Switch off the alert so it stops showing red
options.why: Hides the problem without fixing it.

hints: What does the backup software record when a job fails?
How do you know a backup is actually usable?
Is it safe to remove old backups without checking?
real_world_tip: Test restores regularly, not just after failures. A backup that has never been restored is only a hope.
